💸Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach vividly recalls working on long-term strategy as a new CEO of an iconic company smack in the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic in early 2020.

Inside an empty, sprawling headquarters a few miles from PepsiCo in Purchase, NY and next to a furry friend.

“It was a big learning. One of the things that I picked up was, it's good to be in the office. So every day I drove to the office, including my predecessor, who was our executive chair for a period of time. Every day we showed up here and it was five of us. One gentleman from our canteen company was brave enough to come in in this office,” Miebach told me in a new drop of my Power Players podcast on @YahooFinance from inside that same sprawling headquarters. 

“It was five of us and a security person. One of my colleagues brought his dog because his dog sitter wasn't around any longer. And this was the think tank.”

What a way to start a CEO tenure!

We chatted at length about the future of payments…which is going to be pretty wild because of AI.

And yes, we had the fireplace roaring in the background on what was a rainy day. Love me a good fireplace.

The Nasdaq wants to be the market that never sleeps. 💤

The Nasdaq says it will start trading stocks for 23 hours a day starting December 6.

The move is still subject to SEC approval and comes as the exchange ultimately wants to offer 24/7 trading.

Nasdaq president Tal Cohen says the expansion is a way to "broaden investor access and expand wealth-building opportunities" for everyone.

Rival NYSE has already won SEC approval for a 22-hour day running from 1:30 a.m. to 11:30 p.m.
